To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

novel Ocimumosides A and B isolated from Ocimum sanctum possess anti-stress activity at the level of monoamine neurotransmitters and antioxidant systems in rats subjected to chronic unpredictable stress, which may be useful for the development of novel anti-stress drugs.
Ocimumoside-A and Ocimumosides-B are effective in reversing chronic stress induced changes in brain monoaminergic and oxidative stress markers in rats.
Ocimumoside-A and Ocimumosides B are the first compounds isolated from Ocimum sanctum which have been found to have significant anti-stress activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of novel compounds from OS and their therapeutic importance for the treatment of stress-related disorders.
the development of novel and potent anti-stress agents from the traditional Indian medicinal plant OS.
the isolation, characterization and evaluation of Ocimumoside compounds as anti-stress and antioxidant agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Ocimumoside-A and B, isolated from the ethyl acetate fraction of OS, have a significant anti-stress activity, and this activity is mediated through their modulation of central monoaminergic and oxidative stress mechanisms.

Ocimumoside-A and Ocimumosides B are novel Ocimumosides which are effective in modulating chronic unpredictable stress-induced alterations in the monoamine and antioxidant levels in brain regions and thus, can be considered as potential anti-stress and antioxidant agents.
Ocimumoside-A and B are the novel compounds with anti-stress activity, while Ocimarin has no such activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ocimumoside compounds are the most effective anti-stress and anti-oxidant agents in comparison to Ocimarin, which is a potent anti-stress agent.

Ocimumoside-A and Ocimumosides-B, the two new compounds isolated from the leaves of Ocimum sanctum, have been identified as anti-stress agent by modulating the central monoamines and oxidative stress in the brain of chronic stress model in rat.
Ocimum sanctum is a rich source of compounds with potential anti-stress activity and Ocimumosid A and B could be considered as novel anti-stress agents.

the novel compounds OcimumosideA and B isolated from Ocimum sanctum have the potential to be developed into a novel anti-stress agent.
